reading.title: 꿀벌의 춤 언어
reading.passage: When a honeybee discovers a rich source of nectar, it returns to the hive and performs what scientists call a 'waggle dance.' The dance conveys remarkably precise information: the angle of the dance relative to the vertical comb indicates the direction of the food source relative to the sun, while the duration of the waggle phase signals the distance. Bees watching the dance in the darkness of the hive read these signals through touch and vibration rather than sight. Experiments in which researchers moved feeding stations confirmed that recruits flew to the locations encoded in the dance, not simply to places with floral scent. The waggle dance is therefore often cited as one of the few examples of symbolic communication in non-human animals.

qs.p: 왁글 댄스에서 춤의 각도가 나타내는 것은?
qs.e: angle → direction relative to the sun.

qs.p: 벌들은 어두운 벌집 안에서 춤을 어떻게 읽나요?
qs.e: through touch and vibration rather than sight.

reading.title: 로마의 콘크리트
reading.passage: Modern concrete typically begins to crack within decades, yet many Roman structures, including harbors exposed to seawater for two thousand years, remain intact. The Romans mixed volcanic ash with lime and seawater, producing a mineral called aluminous tobermorite as the material aged. Rather than weakening the structure, chemical reactions between seawater and the ash actually reinforced it over time, filling cracks as they formed. Engineers today study this 'self-healing' property in hopes of producing more durable and environmentally friendly building materials, since modern cement production accounts for roughly eight percent of global carbon dioxide emissions.

qs.e: volcanic ash with lime and seawater.

c: 더 내구성 있고 친환경적인 재료를 위해
qs.e: more durable and environmentally friendly materials.

reading.title: 수면과 기억 강화
reading.passage: A growing body of research indicates that sleep plays an active role in consolidating memories. During slow-wave sleep, the hippocampus repeatedly 'replays' patterns of neural activity associated with recent experiences, gradually transferring information to the neocortex for long-term storage. In one influential study, participants who learned word pairs and then slept recalled significantly more pairs than those who remained awake for the same interval. Notably, the benefit was greatest when sleep occurred shortly after learning. These findings challenge the older view of sleep as a passive state and suggest that students who sacrifice sleep to study may be undermining the very process that stabilizes what they have learned.

qs.p: 서파 수면 중 해마가 하는 일은?

c: 잠을 잔 집단이 더 많이 기억했다
깨어 있던 집단이 더 잘 기억했다
잠을 줄여 공부하면 기억 안정화가 방해될 수 있다

reading.title: 인쇄술과 지식의 확산
reading.passage: The introduction of the movable-type printing press in fifteenth-century Europe transformed the economics of knowledge. Before Gutenberg, producing a single book required months of a scribe's labor, making books luxury items owned mainly by monasteries and wealthy elites. Within fifty years of the press's invention, an estimated twenty million volumes had been printed. Falling prices broadened readership, which in turn created incentives for authors to write in vernacular languages rather than Latin. Historians argue that this feedback loop — cheaper books producing more readers producing more books — accelerated the Reformation, the Scientific Revolution, and ultimately the spread of literacy itself.

qs.e: luxury items owned by monasteries and elites.
incentives to write in vernacular languages.

c: 싼 책 → 더 많은 독자 → 더 많은 책
qs.e: cheaper books producing more readers producing more books.

reading.title: 도시 열섬 현상
reading.passage: Cities are consistently warmer than the rural areas that surround them, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect. Asphalt and concrete absorb solar radiation by day and release it slowly at night, while the scarcity of vegetation reduces cooling through evaporation. Waste heat from vehicles, air conditioners, and industry adds to the burden. The temperature gap, typically one to three degrees Celsius, can exceed ten degrees on calm summer nights. Mitigation strategies include planting street trees, installing reflective 'cool roofs,' and preserving urban parks. Studies show that neighborhoods with abundant tree cover can be several degrees cooler than adjacent districts, which has significant implications for public health during heat waves.

qs.p: 도시가 교외보다 더운 원인이 아닌 것은?

qs.e: several degrees cooler than adjacent districts.

reading.title: 언어 소멸과 다양성
reading.passage: Linguists estimate that of the roughly seven thousand languages spoken today, nearly half may disappear by the end of the century. Languages vanish when children cease to learn them, usually because parents perceive a dominant language as the path to economic opportunity. The loss is not merely sentimental: each language encodes unique knowledge of local ecosystems, medicinal plants, and social history, often unrecorded elsewhere. Revitalization efforts — immersion schools, digital archives, and media in minority languages — have had notable successes, including the revival of Hawaiian and Welsh. Such cases demonstrate that decline is not irreversible when communities and institutions commit resources to transmission.

c: 아이들이 그 언어를 더 이상 배우지 않을 때
qs.e: when children cease to learn them.

qs.p: 언어 소멸이 단순한 감상적 손실이 아닌 이유는?
qs.e: encodes unique knowledge of ecosystems, plants, history.
the revival of Hawaiian and Welsh.

reading.title: 판게아와 대륙 이동
reading.passage: In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined in a single landmass he called Pangaea. He noted that the coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces, that identical fossils appeared on both sides of the Atlantic, and that glacial deposits occurred in now-tropical regions. Yet geologists largely rejected his theory for decades because Wegener could not explain what force moved the continents. The mechanism emerged in the 1960s with the theory of plate tectonics: the discovery of seafloor spreading showed that new crust forms at mid-ocean ridges, pushing plates apart at roughly the speed fingernails grow. Wegener's evidence, once dismissed, is now taught as a classic case of data preceding explanation.

qs.p: 베게너의 이론이 수십 년간 거부된 이유는?
qs.e: could not explain what force moved the continents.

reading.title: 행동경제학과 넛지
reading.passage: Classical economics assumes that individuals weigh costs and benefits rationally, yet behavioral research reveals systematic departures from rationality. People overvalue immediate rewards, follow default options, and are influenced by how choices are framed. 'Nudge' policies exploit these tendencies for public benefit without restricting freedom of choice. When organ donation systems switched from opt-in to opt-out, effective consent rates rose dramatically; when cafeterias placed fruit at eye level, consumption increased. Critics argue that nudging can shade into manipulation, since it operates below conscious awareness. Proponents respond that some choice architecture is unavoidable — every menu has a first item — so designers might as well arrange it to serve people's own long-term interests.

qs.p: 행동경제학이 밝힌 인간의 특징이 아닌 것은?
qs.e: 고전 경제학의 가정이 항상 합리적이라는 것.

lectures.title: 심리학 강의: 기억의 왜곡
lines: Today we'll look at why eyewitness testimony is less reliable than juries tend to assume. Memory is not a video recording. Each time we recall an event, we actually reconstruct it, and new information can slip into the reconstruction. In a famous experiment, participants watched a car accident. Those asked how fast the cars were going when they 'smashed' into each other reported higher speeds than those who heard the word 'hit.' A week later, the 'smashed' group even remembered seeing broken glass — glass that never existed. This is called the misinformation effect, and it has led many courts to treat eyewitness accounts with greater caution.

qs.e: remembered broken glass that never existed.

lectures.title: 생물학 강의: 문어의 위장
lines: Octopuses are masters of disguise, and what makes this remarkable is that they are almost certainly colorblind. Their skin contains thousands of pigment sacs called chromatophores, each controlled by muscles and nerves, which expand or contract to change color in a fraction of a second. Beneath these lie reflective cells that mimic the brightness and texture of the surroundings. So how does a colorblind animal match colors it cannot see? One hypothesis is that light-sensitive proteins in the skin itself allow the octopus to 'see' with its body. The debate is ongoing, but it reminds us that vision, in the broadest sense, need not be confined to eyes.

lectures.title: 역사 강의: 실크로드
lines: When we say 'Silk Road,' the singular is misleading. It was a shifting network of caravan routes linking China to the Mediterranean, and silk was only one of many goods. Paper, spices, glassware, and horses moved along it — but so did ideas. Buddhism traveled from India into China along these routes, and centuries later, technologies like papermaking moved west, reaching Europe through the Islamic world. Of course, the network also carried disease; many historians believe the plague of the fourteenth century followed trade routes into Europe. So the Silk Road is best understood not as a road at all, but as history's first great information superhighway — with all the benefits and risks that implies.

qs.p: 강사가 '실크로드'라는 이름이 오해를 부른다고 한 이유는?
qs.e: a shifting network, not a single road.
Buddhism traveled from India into China.

lectures.title: 환경과학 강의: 산호 백화
lines: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all marine species. The coral animal itself is nearly transparent; its brilliant colors come from microscopic algae living inside its tissues. The algae photosynthesize and share nutrients with the coral — a textbook case of mutualism. But this partnership is temperature-sensitive. When water warms by even one or two degrees for several weeks, corals expel their algae and turn bone white, a process called bleaching. Bleached corals are not dead, but they are starving, and if the heat persists they die. That's why marine biologists treat mass bleaching events as early warning systems for ocean warming.

c: 산호가 조류를 내보내 하얗게 되는 것
qs.e: expel their algae and turn white.

lectures.title: 천문학 강의: 외계 행성 찾기
lines: How do we find planets orbiting stars light-years away, when the star outshines the planet a billion to one? Mostly, we don't look for the planet at all — we watch the star. In the transit method, we measure the star's brightness continuously; if a planet crosses in front, the light dips by a tiny, regular amount. The size of the dip tells us the planet's diameter, and the interval between dips gives its orbital period. The radial velocity method instead watches the star wobble: an orbiting planet tugs its star back and forth, shifting the starlight's color slightly toward blue, then red. Combining both methods yields the planet's density — and that tells us whether we're looking at a gas giant or a rocky world like our own.

qs.e: light dips by a tiny, regular amount.
an orbiting planet tugs its star.

qs.p: 두 방법을 결합하면 알 수 있는 것은?

lectures.title: 예술사 강의: 인상주의의 탄생
lines: In 1874, a group of painters rejected by the official Paris Salon organized their own exhibition. A critic, mocking Monet's 'Impression, Sunrise,' called them mere 'impressionists' — and the insult became a movement's name. What made their work radical? First, they left the studio to paint outdoors, capturing changing light directly. Second, new chemistry gave them portable paint tubes and brighter pigments. Third, they painted modern life — railway stations, cafés, weekend crowds — subjects the academy considered vulgar. Within a generation, the outsiders had redefined what painting could be, and the Salon that rejected them became a historical footnote.

qs.e: portable paint tubes and brighter pigments.

vocabq.p: The results were consistent across all trials, ___ the hypothesis.
vocabq.e:
📌 corroborate = 확증하다. 모든 실험에서 결과가 '일치'했으니 가설을 뒷받침(확증)하는 문맥이에요.
✘ contradicting(모순되는)은 정반대, abandoning(버리는)·delaying(지연시키는)은 결과가 일치하는 상황과 논리가 안 맞아요.

vocabq.p: The drug's effects ___ within hours, requiring repeated doses.
vocabq.e:
📌 dissipate = 흩어져 사라지다. '반복 투여가 필요하다' = 효과가 몇 시간 안에 사라진다는 뜻.
✘ accumulate(축적되다)면 오히려 투여를 줄여야 하고, solidify(굳다)·originate(비롯되다)는 약효 소멸과 무관해요.

vocabq.p: Her argument was so ___ that even critics were persuaded.
vocabq.e:
📌 compelling = 설득력 있는. '비판자들마저 설득됐다'는 결과가 단서예요.
✘ tedious(지루한)·obscure(모호한)·fragile(허술한) 주장이라면 비판자를 설득할 수 없었겠죠.

vocabq.p: The species shows a ___ preference for shallow, warm waters.
vocabq.e:
📌 marked = 뚜렷한, 현저한 (mark '표시'에서 온 뜻 — 표시가 날 만큼 분명한).
✘ negligible(무시해도 될 정도의)은 반대 뜻, reluctant(꺼리는)는 사람 심리에, hollow(속 빈)는 물체에 쓰는 말이에요.

vocabq.p: The two theories are not mutually ___; both may be partly true.
vocabq.e:
📌 mutually exclusive = 상호 배타적(하나가 맞으면 다른 건 틀림). '둘 다 부분적으로 맞을 수 있다'가 힌트!
✘ inclusive(포괄적)·productive(생산적)·attractive(매력적)는 mutually와 이 관용 표현을 만들지 않아요.

vocabq.p: Fossil evidence ___ the claim that birds descended from dinosaurs.
vocabq.e:
📌 substantiate = (증거로) 입증하다. substance(실체)를 부여한다는 어원 그대로예요.
✘ undermine(약화시키다)은 반대 방향, ridicule(조롱하다)·postpone(미루다)은 증거-주장 관계에 안 맞아요.

vocabq.p: The committee reached a decision only after ___ deliberation.
vocabq.e:
📌 lengthy deliberation = 오랜 숙고. 'only after(~한 후에야)'가 오래 걸렸다는 힌트예요.
✘ instant(즉각적인)면 only after와 모순, absent(부재한)·casual(건성의) 숙고 끝의 결정이란 것도 어색해요.

vocabq.p: Rising temperatures could ___ the melting of polar ice.
vocabq.e:
📌 accelerate = 가속하다. 기온 상승 → 해빙이 빨라진다는 인과관계.
✘ decelerate(감속하다)·terminate(끝내다)는 온난화 문맥과 반대, imitate(모방하다)는 의미 자체가 안 통해요.

vocabq.p: The findings must be interpreted with ___, given the small sample.
vocabq.e:
📌 with caution = 신중하게. '표본이 작다(given the small sample)'는 단서가 신중함을 요구해요.
✘ certainty(확신)·haste(서두름)는 작은 표본과 정반대 태도, applause(박수)는 해석 방식이 아니에요.

vocabq.p: The ancient text was ___ deciphered after decades of effort.
vocabq.e:
📌 finally = 마침내. '수십 년의 노력 끝에'와 자연스럽게 이어져요.
✘ barely never·scarcely not은 이중 부정으로 문법 자체가 깨졌고, formerly(이전에)는 시간 논리가 안 맞아요.

vocabq.p: Urban expansion continues to ___ on natural habitats.
vocabq.e:
📌 encroach on = (영역을) 잠식하다, 침범하다. 도시 확장이 서식지를 갉아먹는 문맥.
✘ reflect on(숙고하다)·insist on(고집하다)·depend on(의존하다)은 모두 on을 받지만 뜻이 전혀 달라요 — 전치사만 보고 고르면 함정!

vocabq.p: The study's conclusions are ___ on several untested assumptions.
vocabq.e:
📌 contingent on = ~에 좌우되는, 달려 있는. 검증 안 된 가정 위에 서 있다는 뜻.
✘ independent(독립적인)는 반대 뜻이고, abundant(풍부한)·generous(후한)는 on과 이 구조를 못 만들어요.

vocabq.p: The professor asked us to ___ the main argument in one sentence.
vocabq.e:
📌 distill = (증류하듯) 핵심만 추려내다. '한 문장으로'가 압축의 힌트예요.
✘ dilute(희석하다)는 오히려 묽게 만드는 것, discard(버리다)·disturb(방해하다)는 요약과 무관해요.

vocabq.p: Genetic mutations arise ___, without regard to their usefulness.
vocabq.e:
📌 randomly = 무작위로. 'without regard to usefulness(유용성과 무관하게)'가 무작위성의 단서.
✘ deliberately(의도적으로)는 정확히 반대예요 — 돌연변이에는 의도가 없다는 게 진화론의 핵심!

vocabq.p: The bridge's design must ___ extreme wind conditions.
vocabq.e:
📌 withstand = 견뎌내다 (with-'맞서'+stand'서다').
✘ surrender(굴복하다)는 설계 목적과 반대, postpone(미루다)·diminish(줄이다)는 바람을 목적어로 받기에 어색해요.

vocabq.p: The two languages, though related, are mutually ___.
vocabq.e:
📌 mutually unintelligible = 서로 알아들을 수 없는. though related(친족 언어인데도)와 대조되는 사실.
✘ audible(들리는)은 물리적 소리 얘기고, fluent는 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요.

vocabq.p: Sea levels are rising at an ___ rate.
vocabq.e:
📌 unprecedented = 전례 없는 (un+precedent'선례'). at an unprecedented rate는 논문·뉴스 단골 연어예요.
✘ invisible(보이지 않는)·optional(선택적인) rate는 성립하지 않는 조합이에요.

vocabq.p: The theory ___ elegantly for the observed anomalies.
vocabq.e:
📌 account for = ~을 설명하다. 이론이 변칙 현상들을 깔끔하게 설명한다는 뜻.
✘ blame(탓하다)·search(찾다)는 for를 받아도 뜻이 안 통하고, argues against면 이론이 스스로를 반박하는 꼴이에요.

vocabq.p: Scholars continue to ___ over the manuscript's authorship.
vocabq.e:
📌 dispute over = ~을 두고 논쟁하다. continue to(계속)와 저자 논란이라는 문맥이 단서.
✘ agree(동의하다)면 논란이 끝난 것이고, celebrate(기념하다)·rehearse(연습하다)는 over와 안 어울려요.

vocabq.p: Efficient irrigation can ___ the effects of drought.
vocabq.e:
📌 mitigate = 완화하다. 관개시설이 가뭄 피해를 '줄이는' 문맥.
✘ aggravate(악화시키다)는 정반대! mitigate↔aggravate는 토플 단골 반의어 짝이에요.

vocabq.p: The data reveal a ___ decline in insect populations.
vocabq.e:
📌 precipitous = 가파른, 급격한 (precipice'절벽'에서 온 말 — 절벽처럼 떨어지는).
✘ gentle rise of는 decline(감소)과 모순, welcome(반가운) 감소도 곤충 감소 문맥에 안 맞아요.

vocabq.p: His later work ___ significantly from his early style.
vocabq.e:
📌 diverge from = ~에서 갈라지다, 달라지다 (di-'따로'+verge'향하다').
✘ borrow from(빌리다)이면 오히려 비슷해진다는 뜻이고, profit/suffer from은 스타일 변화 문맥에 안 맞아요.

vocabq.p: The immune system can ___ between harmless and dangerous bacteria.
vocabq.e:
📌 discriminate between A and B = A와 B를 구별하다 (차별이 아니라 '식별'이 원뜻!).
✘ circulate(순환하다)·evaporate(증발하다)·negotiate(협상하다)는 between과 이 구조를 못 만들어요.

vocabq.p: The historian offered a ___ account of the war's causes.
vocabq.e:
📌 nuanced = 미묘한 차이까지 담은, 섬세한. 학술 서평에서 최고의 칭찬 중 하나예요.
✘ careless(부주의한)는 폄하하는 말, silent(침묵의)·monotone(단조로운) account는 어색한 조합이에요.
